blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover (Figure 1, steps 3 and 4); Guarantees (ZG-3)
blocking.issue: The new process joins every SO_REUSEPORT group before it is ready or accepted. A TCP socket that listens is in the kernel's reuseport hash at once, so about half of new client connections, and about half of the balancer's new 9901 probe connections, reach a process that is still warming, may still be refused because of a digest change, and may exit after the 60 s timeout. On the refusal and timeout paths, the new process exits with connections still queued on its sockets. That is exactly the failure that HAProxy measured and that this document cites as the reason for CBPF steering: 155 failures per million from sockets closed with queued connections. Probes that reach the new process before it is accepted see a process that is not the lock holder, so the Node's /readyz is not 200 throughout. This breaks the readiness gating of ADR-0015 (pack section 7, Upgrades row: the new process reports ready over a Unix socket before it takes traffic) and ZG-3. At 10x scale, V-3's 1,000 handovers under load would each place connections in queues that nobody accepts whenever a handover is refused after binding (a digest race during a Rollout) or times out.
blocking.evidence: Figure 1: "New->>K: bind 8080, 8443 and 9901 with SO_REUSEPORT" followed by "New->>New: warm pools, readiness checks pass" and "alt unknown format marker, digest differs, or timeout ... Old-->>New: refused, New exits". Step 3: "It binds 8080, 8443 and 9901 with `SO_REUSEPORT` (in-flight QUIC on UDP 8443 is lost), warms, then reports version, format markers and active digest". Step 4: "A new process not accepted within 60 s (target) exits". ZG-3: "An in-place handover refuses no new TCP connection and keeps the Node's `/readyz` at 200 throughout".
blocking.fix: Split bind from listen. In step 3, the new process binds 8080, 8443 and 9901 with SO_REUSEPORT to detect port errors, but it calls listen() only after the old process accepts its ready message. After that, the old process attaches CBPF steering and closes its listeners (steps 5 and 6). State that the old process's /readyz answers every probe until steering is attached, and that a refusal or timeout exits a process that holds no listening socket, so no connection is ever queued to it. Update Figure 1 (move the listen arrow after "accepted") and add a V-3 variant that refuses or times out 1,000 handovers under S1 with zero refused connections (target). Replace text rather than add, because about 235 words of headroom remain under the 4,500-word maximum.

blocking.section: Binary upgrades > Drain timeline defaults; In-place handover (Figure 1)
blocking.issue: The Drain assumes that balancers stop sending within the fixed 5 s accept window, but nothing bounds the balancer's detection time. External L4 balancers mark a target down only after their probe interval times their unhealthy threshold. After second 5 the old process closes its listeners, so every new connection the balancer sends in the rest of that detection time is refused. This happens on every T5 Drain-and-restart, on every scale-in (Scalability, Warm-up: "Scale-in is a Drain") and on edge sites. Across a fleet it means refused connections on every Node that scales in, which contradicts V-4 ("Zero failed new requests") and CE-2. In a handover, the old process fails /readyz while a balancer that reuses a keep-alive probe connection to the old process's 9901 keeps probing it, because CBPF steers only new connections. That balancer marks the Node down even though the new process serves, which contradicts ZG-3.
blocking.evidence: Drain table: "| 0 to 5 s | Accept window while balancers observe `/readyz`; skipped in a handover | 5 s (target) |"; text: "the accept window covers external balancers probing `/readyz`". Figure 1: "Old->>Old: accept the queued connections, close listeners, fail readyz". V-4 pass: "Zero failed new requests; exit within 30 s (target)".
blocking.fix: Add a MUST: balancer probe interval times unhealthy threshold stays at or below the accept window, 5 s (target). Otherwise the operator lengthens the accept window, which OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-1 must then allow, and the Drain deadline and grace figures move with it. Add a verification row that checks the balancer's detection time. For a handover, state that the old process never answers 503 to probes. Instead, at steering time it closes idle 9901 connections and sends `Connection: close` on the next 9901 response, so the next probe opens a new connection that CBPF steers to the new process. Keep ZG-3 and V-3's "200 throughout" and make the mechanism say how that is achieved.

blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover (step 6 and the paragraph after it); Kubernetes replacement; Control plane upgrades; Verification runbook (V-3, V-5)
blocking.issue: Every Node upgrade and every Ruralz Control replica replacement resets Control Streams, but the document ignores the effect on the published Node count. Control plane and GitOps counts only ready Nodes that stayed connected for 10 minutes (target), publishes large decreases at once, and raises the count by at most 10% per minute. A handover sends a `draining` Heartbeat, so the Node leaves the count at once. The new process's stream starts at age 0, so the Node rejoins the count only after 10 minutes plus the ramp. A Kubernetes replacement of one zone's share (L4X-6), or an in-place fleet upgrade finished in under 10 minutes, therefore drops clusterNodeCount by a third, or toward zero. Derived per-Node ceilings then rise to limit / count, or to the full limit. Scalability names this failure: "a near-zero count sends derived ceilings to the full limit, multiplying hot-key GCRA calls". Hot-key shards open their breakers, and co-tenant keys fall back to failureMode. The fail-open bound N_serving x max(1, 2 x requests / N_published) grows by the same factor, and recovery takes about 34 minutes (hypothesis, the Scalability lagging-count row). A Ruralz Control rolling upgrade restarts every stream up to three times. The document only asks for Raft catch-up between replicas, and V-5 checks no count or breaker criterion, although CE-7 and CE-10 do. The handover paragraph claims that the only exposure is "one 15 s heartbeat interval".
blocking.evidence: Step 6: "At Drain start the old process sends a last `Heartbeat` with `draining`, closes its Control Stream and releases the lock. The new process takes the lock and dials 8091 with `Hello`". "derived ceilings use the full limit until its first `HeartbeatReply`, within one 15 s heartbeat interval (target)". Control plane step 2: "wait for `/readyz` on 9902 and Raft catch-up before the next". V-5 pass: "Zero request errors; no Node unready". Control plane and GitOps, Replica roles: "`clusterNodeCount` counts ready Nodes that ACKed a Revision and stayed connected 10 minutes (target); large decreases publish at once, and increases rise at most 10% per minute".
blocking.fix: Add a short "Node count during upgrades" paragraph with a bound. Until OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 (a) keys qualification by `node.id`, upgrades MUST pace so that at most 10% of a Cluster's Nodes are unqualified at once (target). For 1,000 Nodes that means at least about 100 minutes (hypothesis). Add an Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops: a handover `Hello` for the same `node.id`, and a handover `draining` Heartbeat, keep the Node's qualification. Between replica replacements, wait until `ruralz_control_connected_nodes` has recovered. Add pass criteria to V-3 and V-5: `ruralz_control_cluster_nodes` drops by at most 10% (target) and no State client breaker opens, matching CE-7 and CE-10. Also mention the node_count_unknown fail-open clamp max(1, requests / 100) (target) for the new process.

blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover (overlap sizing); path table
blocking.issue: The overlap sizing counts only a second base RSS and Plugin pools. Every Node ceiling, however, is per process. For up to 25 s the old process keeps its established and long-lived connections (up to 20,000 TLS connections at 96 KiB, about 1.9 GiB (target)), its in-flight buffers (512 MiB `maxBufferedBytes`), its (K + 2) snapshots and state tables of up to about 475 MiB. Meanwhile the new process accepts every new connection up to its own 20,000 and reserves its own Plugin instances at full limits against its own 2 GiB cap. Two independent GOMEMLIMITs at about 90% of the container or unit memory (Scalability, Scale unit) add up to about 180% of a limit that both processes share. The kernel, not the Go GC, then decides, and an OOM kill of either process drops in-flight requests. That breaks ZG-3 and the "Capacity ... Unchanged" claim. The State client also doubles: 2 pipelined plus 8 dedicated connections per shard per process. Upgrading one zone's share of a 1,000-Node Cell adds about 3,330 connections per shard (hypothesis). That exceeds a server client limit sized at 10 x N_serving, which Scalability makes a MUST above 900 Nodes, so connections are refused, breakers open after 5 connect failures and keys fall back to failureMode.
blocking.evidence: "During the overlap both processes hold a snapshot, Plugin pools and their own `GOMEMLIMIT`, so handover hosts SHOULD keep free memory for a second base RSS, 100 MB plus 2 KB per Route (target), plus its Plugin pools (OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-6)." Path table: "| In-place handover | ... | Unchanged; the Node stays ready |".
blocking.fix: Restate the overlap peak as the old process's loaded working set, which falls to zero by the Drain deadline, plus the new process's base RSS, snapshot, Plugin reservations and the connection and buffer memory for the connections it accepts within 25 s, all as (hypothesis), with a worked figure at 20,000 TLS connections. Add the doubled State client connections and require the server client limit to cover 10 x (N_serving + Nodes in handover) (target). Either lower each process's GOMEMLIMIT and connection ceiling during the overlap, or require handover hosts to be sized for two processes, and record the chosen option in OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-6. Add a V-3 pass criterion: no OOM kill and no State Store connection refusal.

blocking.section: Guarantees (ZG-1); Configuration hot reload > Atomic swap
blocking.issue: ZG-1 misstates the retirement rule of Data plane and of this document's own Atomic swap text. When a snapshot becomes closing at the (K + 1)th retirement, its streams end at once, with no grace. The 30 s grace applies only to non-stream requests, which then end with RZ-RT-014. So a Hot Reload can end in-flight requests, and "drops no in-flight request" is false. The scale risk is also unaddressed. In an `all-at-once` Rollout, or in file mode where every Node watches one directory, the third activation within one session lifetime closes every WebSocket, SSE and gRPC stream older than three Revisions on every Node in the same second, with no jitter. At 20,000 sessions per Node (target) and 1,000 Nodes, that is up to 20 million simultaneous reconnects (hypothesis) against TLS handshakes, JWKS verification and first-seen GCRA budgets. A rollback plus a re-rollout, which is routine, is enough to reach three activations. The Drain spreads going-away signals over a 10 s window, but retirement does not.
blocking.evidence: ZG-1: "A Hot Reload drops no in-flight request; only a stream that outlives K + 1 further activations and a 30 s grace ends, K = 2 (target)". Atomic swap: "a third retirement closes the oldest one's streams (WebSocket 1001, gRPC `UNAVAILABLE`, SSE end with a retry hint) and ends the rest after a 30 s grace (target) with `RZ-RT-014`".
blocking.fix: Rewrite ZG-1: "A Hot Reload ends no in-flight request unless K + 1 = 3 further activations happen during its lifetime (target). Then its streams close at once with a reconnect signal, and other requests end after a 30 s grace with RZ-RT-014." Add a sentence with the reconnect burst at one Cluster (hypothesis). Add an Open question owned by data-plane: spread closing-snapshot stream ends over the 10 s jitter window (target), as the Drain does. Add a V-1 case with three Rollouts in quick succession and 20,000 sessions, which passes when reconnects stay spread over the window.

blocking.section: Binary upgrades (path table); Binary upgrades > Kubernetes replacement; Long-lived WebSocket and SSE connections
blocking.issue: The replacement path contradicts Deployment topologies, which sets the Node StatefulSet to `RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable` matching the PodDisruptionBudget, one zone's share at minimum scale (target). PodDisruptionBudgets bound evictions, not the StatefulSet controller's own updates. Under the topology as configured, one step takes out a whole zone's share, not one Pod. That share consumes the same zone-loss headroom that Scalability sizes for (survivors under 80% CPU). A real zone failure during a step therefore removes 2/Z of capacity, two thirds at Z = 3, and the survivors shed with RZ-RT-005. The reconnect math also changes. The document's "about 2,000 reconnects per second" per Node becomes one zone's share times 2,000, about 666,000 per second at 1,000 Nodes (hypothesis), landing on the remaining two thirds of Nodes. Read literally as one Pod at a time, a 1,000-Node Cluster takes about 12.5 hours (hypothesis) at 45 s per step, which the document never states.
blocking.evidence: Path table: "| Replacement | Kubernetes (T4) | StatefulSet rolling update: preStop, Drain, new Pod | One Pod at a time, within the PodDisruptionBudget |". Kubernetes replacement: "Each step removes one Pod for about 40 to 45 s (hypothesis), so `minReplicas` SHOULD hold one zone's share of headroom." Deployment topologies: "`RollingUpdate`, `maxUnavailable` matching the PodDisruptionBudget" and "for Nodes, one zone's share at minimum scale (target)".
blocking.fix: Align the text with Deployment topologies: at most one zone's share per step, and state the upgrade duration (steps x 45 s, hypothesis). Quantify the Cluster-wide reconnect rate at one zone's share and the absorbing load on the survivors. Add a rule: before a T4 upgrade, scale out by one zone's share or confirm that surplus capacity covers it (target), and halt the update on a zone incident, so that an upgrade and a zone loss together stay within the 80% CPU sizing. Tie this to L4X-3, since a zone-share step also moves the published Node count.

blocking.section: Control plane upgrades (Prepare step, skew table); Verification runbook (Before row)
blocking.issue: The version skew does not match Release, versioning and compatibility, which acceptance criterion 3 requires. Release classes a Node newer than the Control Store version as outside policy. Its Figure 2 also requires every Node at N-1 ("Upgrade lagging Nodes to N-1") before the first replica is replaced. This document's Prepare step and runbook admit Nodes already at N, and its skew row for Nodes within one Cluster drops the outside-policy condition. A Node at N ahead of Ruralz Control can report schema levels that Ruralz Control cannot interpret. An operator following this runbook can also upgrade Nodes first and then find that a replica rollback or a restore leaves Nodes outside policy.
blocking.evidence: Prepare: "Every replica reported a snapshot at the Control Store version and every Node runs N-1 or N". Skew table: "| Nodes within one Cluster | Any mix of N and N-1 |". Runbook: "| Before | `ruralz version`; `ruralz node list --cluster <name>` | Every Node at N-1 or N; digests equal the promoted digest |". Release: "Nodes within one Cluster | Any mix of N and N-1 | N-2 or older; newer than the Control Store version".
blocking.fix: Prepare: "every Node runs N-1, the Control Store version; upgrade lagging Nodes first". Skew row: "Any mix of N and N-1, never newer than the Control Store version". Runbook Before row for a Ruralz Control upgrade: "Every Node at N-1". Keep the generic N-1-or-N wording only for a Node upgrade after finalize.

blocking.issue: Rollback after finalize cites rule 6 of Ruralz Control upgrades but describes rule 5, the restore. It also omits the two steps that rule 6 assigns to this document: while still on N, roll out a Revision without N-only fields to every Cluster until `complete`, then return every Node to N-1 by handover, and only then restore. Figure 4 sends a finalized Ruralz Control straight to "Restore". If Nodes already run N, restoring an N-1 Control Store leaves them newer than the Control Store version, which is outside policy. Their Last-Known-Good may also hold N-only fields that N-1 cannot boot (RZ-CFG-024), so every Node restarted during the recovery stays not ready. That is an availability failure across every Cell the deployment serves. Separately, the path past the binary rollback limit (r5 then r4) chains a three-step Revision revert with a two-step binary rollback, five steps in all. That contradicts ZG-8 and acceptance criterion 4.
blocking.evidence: "After finalize, returning to N-1 is a restore into an empty N-1 deployment that loses later writes and leaves Nodes detached until a revocation list arrives (rule 6 of [Ruralz Control upgrades](...))". Figure 4: `q5 -- "yes" --> r7` and `r5 --> r4`. ZG-8: "Every rollback this document owns takes three steps or fewer".
blocking.fix: Add a rollback row, "Ruralz Control after finalize, Nodes at N", with three steps: (1) roll out a Revision without N-only fields to every Cluster and wait for `complete`; (2) hand every Node back to N-1; (3) restore, as High availability and disaster recovery describes. Cite it as rule 6, and describe the Nodes-still-at-N-1 case as rule 5. In Figure 4, route "finalized" through "Nodes at N?" to the new row. Either make the past-the-limit binary path one three-step row (Revision revert with `--wait`, handover to N-1, confirm), or scope ZG-8 to single-change rollbacks and say that the combined path is two rollbacks.

blocking.section: State Store upgrades (table and the paragraph after it); Verification runbook (V-7)
blocking.issue: The planned-upgrade row states its accuracy cost as "within bounds" with no number. It does not sequence shards, and it treats a planned change like an unplanned failover. Scalability quantifies a failover with replication lag L as L x the key's admitted rate extra, 100 at 1,000 per second and 100 ms lag (hypothesis). A key first written within the lag restarts with a full tau, up to `requests` extra, and Token Budgets overspend up to L x reserved tokens per second per key. None of this appears. For a Cell at the 16-shard ceiling, failing shards over together puts the whole Cell in failureMode for about 15 s. Failing them over one at a time costs 16 x 15 s, about 4 minutes of `closed` Token Budget 503s spread across keys (hypothesis). The document gives neither figure. While the upgraded replica is down, a zone loss that takes the primary leaves no failover target, which turns an upgrade into a Cell outage for as long as it lasts. V-7 also drops CE-5's scale and reconnect criteria (at least 100 Nodes, every Node reconnected within 10 s).
blocking.evidence: "| Server patch or minor upgrade | Upgrade the replica, fail over, upgrade the former primary; one Cell at a time, off peak | `failureMode` for about 15 s per failover (hypothesis): Rate Limits fail open within bounds, `closed` Token Budgets return 503 `RZ-STS`; scripts reload on reconnect |". V-7: "| V-7 | CE-5: State Store primary killed | `failureMode` for at most 15 s (target) | Planned (M1) |".
blocking.fix: Say "one shard at a time within a Cell". Before failover, wait until the replica has caught up with the primary, so that planned lag is near zero (target). Replace "within bounds" with the Scalability failover rows (L x rate; up to `requests` for keys first written within the lag; Token Budget L x reserved tokens per second), and state the per-Cell degraded time as shards x 15 s (hypothesis). Add: upgrade a replica only while a second replica, or the primary's zone, is healthy, and pause on a zone incident. Align V-7 with CE-5: at least 100 Nodes (target), every Node reconnected within 10 s (target), and extra admissions within the lag bound.

blocking.issue: Step 7 contradicts two documents. The Configuration model requires the artifact's requested Capabilities to be a subset of `spec.capabilities`, not equal to them. Release, versioning and compatibility (Plugin ABI versioning rule 2) says that an ABI level above the Node's is a NACK that Ruralz Control cannot reproduce, so it quarantines the Node as transient. This document classes every mismatch as deterministic. The scale consequence: in a Cluster that mixes N and N-1 Nodes, which the skew policy allows indefinitely, a Rollout of a Plugin that needs the N ABI level quarantines every N-1 Node. When more than max(1, 5% of the batch) of the Nodes are N-1, the batch fails and the Rollout is rolled back or paused. Operators get no warning from this section, because the document calls the failure deterministic.
blocking.evidence: "| 7 | Plugin artifacts fetched by digest, signed, with ABI, Phases and Capabilities equal to `Plugin.spec` and an ABI level at or below the Node's ([ADR-0005](../adr/0005-plugin-abi-v1.md)) | RZ-CFG-028, RZ-CFG-033 | Deterministic for a mismatch; transient for a fetch failure |". Configuration model: "its requested Capabilities are a subset of `spec.capabilities`".
blocking.fix: Change the row to "ABI and Phases equal to `Plugin.spec`, requested Capabilities a subset of it, ABI level at or below the Node's". Classify it as "Deterministic for a spec mismatch; transient (quarantine) for an ABI level above the Node's until OQ-release-versioning-and-compatibility-4 closes, and for a fetch failure". Add a sentence repeating Release's MUST NOT: never roll out a Plugin needing a level that some Node of the Cluster lacks.

blocking.issue: The Zero-Downtime Upgrade row changes the meaning of the binding pack section 11 definition. The pack allows rewording only when the meaning is unchanged. The added clause brings a Kubernetes Pod replacement under the term, but a replacement neither binds with SO_REUSEPORT beside the old process nor reports ready before the old one Drains: the old Pod Drains first. That blurs the distinction this lens relies on. An in-place handover keeps capacity, while a replacement removes one zone's share (L4X-6).
blocking.evidence: "| Zero-Downtime Upgrade | Replacing the `ruralzd` binary: the new process binds with `SO_REUSEPORT` and reports ready, then the old process Drains; in place this is a handover, on Kubernetes a Pod replacement |".
blocking.fix: Restore the pack section 11 text verbatim and describe the Kubernetes path separately, for example as "Kubernetes replacement, which is a Drain followed by a new Pod, not a Zero-Downtime Upgrade in the pack sense", or propose a pack amendment through an Open question.

non_blocking.suggestion: The Convert command omits `--environments`, which the CLI reference requires for `--api-version` conversion (it renders both trees per Environment). As written, it exits 2. Use `ruralz bundle render --api-version ruralz/v1beta1 --output-dir <dir> --environments <file>`.

"None with mixed N-1 and N Nodes" leaves out Release's alternative Quota path: up to 2 x `limit` for one window per Node without the switch signal, for example a detached Node (hypothesis). Name both paths.

State the full Scalability bound for a new Cell: one extra `limit` per open window for windows up to 720 h (target). A monthly spend-bearing Quota gets a whole extra allowance, so point to Region-pinned tenants or the Divided pattern for AI spend.

non_blocking.section: Binary upgrades > Long-lived WebSocket and SSE connections
non_blocking.suggestion: AI completions over SSE are cut at the 20 s Drain deadline (target) and charged the full reservation R. Long reasoning completions routinely exceed 20 s, so a fleet upgrade over-charges every such stream by R minus usage and truncates it. Give an expected count or over-charge (hypothesis), and list a longer AI Drain deadline as an option in OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-1.

At 10,000 Nodes (target), an `all-at-once` Rollout of a new Plugin digest makes every Node pull from the registry at once. Rate-limited pulls become transient NACKs, then quarantine, and can fail the batch. Point to Deployment topologies' regional mirror rule and apply it to Plugin artifacts.

When pools warm to 0 at the memory cap, an auth or authz Plugin fails closed (401 or 403) on new requests after an ACKed Rollout. Recommend that canary gates count `RZ-PLG-004` and `RZ-PLG-005`, or that auth and authz pools that cannot warm to at least 1 NACK.

non_blocking.section: Configuration hot reload > Hot Reload versus restart
non_blocking.suggestion: Changing a `ratelimit` Policy's `requests` starts fresh GCRA state and briefly admits 2 x limit (Traffic management, Decision path). Add this to the Hot Reload effects so operators do not read it as a zero-cost change.

With three voters, a zone loss during a replica replacement loses quorum (1 of 3 remain). Recommend five voters for Clusters that upgrade during business hours, or pausing the upgrade on any zone incident, and say that Nodes keep serving throughout.

V-5 runs at 100 Nodes. Add an F2-scale run (10,000 Nodes, target) or reference F2 and CE-10, because shedding and stream re-homing at ceil(N / 5,000) + 1 replicas (hypothesis) only show near capacity. "None shed" is also unrealistic at exactly the formula's replica count: loosen it to "shed Nodes reconnect within 5 minutes (target)".
SO_REUSEPORT requires only the same effective user ID. Reword so that the man7 citation does not appear to require the same RURALZ_CONFIG and RURALZ_DATA_DIR.

The research file notes that the Kubernetes version in which the preStop `sleep` handler became GA was not verified. Add an Open question or a minimum-version note before relying on it for Planned (M2).

A wrong Environment or Cluster binding is reported as RZ-CFG-033, the signature-failure code. Consider an Open question for a dedicated code owned by configuration-model, so that dashboards do not count binding errors as signature failures.
The body is about 4,265 words against the 4,500 maximum. Apply the fixes above by replacing sentences, not appending them, and do not remove text that resolved earlier findings.

ac_results.ac: Binary upgrades states the drain timeline defaults (readiness failure, preStop, drain timeout, HTTP/2 GOAWAY) with values tagged (target).
ac_results.note: The Drain timeline table and Figure 2 give every value tagged (target). Balancer detection time is unbounded (L4X-2).

ac_results.ac: Binary upgrades defines the strategy for long-lived WebSocket and SSE connections.
ac_results.note: The per-traffic table and the jitter window are present. Zone-share reconnect math is missing (L4X-6), and snapshot-retirement closes have no jitter (L4X-5).

ac_results.ac: Control plane upgrades covers Raft rolling upgrades, and the version skew matches docs/engineering/04-release-versioning-and-compatibility.md (N and N-1).
ac_results.note: Raft rolling upgrades are covered, but the Prepare step, the skew row and the runbook admit Nodes at N before the upgrade, which Release forbids (L4X-7).

ac_results.ac: Rollback takes three steps or fewer.
ac_results.note: The path past the binary rollback limit chains to five steps, and the rule 6 path after finalize is missing (L4X-8).

ac_results.ac: Configuration hot reload enumerates the validation gate checks and covers atomic swap, partial failure and Plugin hot-swap.
ac_results.note: An 11-step gate table, atomic swap, a partial failure table and Plugin hot-swap are present. Step 7 contradicts the Configuration model and Release (L4X-10), and ZG-1 misstates the retirement rule (L4X-5).

ac_results.ac: Binary upgrades follows ADR-0015 (SO_REUSEPORT, drain and readiness gating, no socket passing).
ac_results.note: SO_REUSEPORT, the Drain and the absence of socket passing are present, but the new process listens before it is ready or accepted, so readiness gating does not gate traffic (L4X-1).

foundation_amendments: Pack section 7, Upgrades row (ADR-0015): add "the new process binds but calls listen() only after the old process accepts its readiness message, so it takes no connection before it is ready", so that readiness gating is enforceable at the socket level (L4X-1).

Pack section 8.8 or 8.11, through OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 and -14: state that a Zero-Downtime Upgrade keeps a Node's `node.id` qualified in the published Node count, so that fleet upgrades cannot collapse derived per-Node ceilings (L4X-3).
